idiom_name: enum (or trait object) dispatch plus per-table Diesel/sqlx row structs
implementation_notes: Rust's type system has no inheritance, so the mapper hierarchy becomes an enum of the hierarchy's variants (or a boxed trait object) plus one row struct per table: Diesel maps each struct to exactly one table via #[diesel(table_name = ...)] and documents only child-to-parent belongs_to associations, so a class-table hierarchy is loaded by a join or two queries and assembled in a mapper function, while a single-table schema maps to one enum matched on the discriminator column. Hand-written mapper functions compose these pieces; no ORM generates a mapper hierarchy for a Rust type hierarchy.
pitfalls: Diesel checks queries against the schema at compile time, so a mapper cannot drift from the table - but hand-written SQL (diesel::sql_query) escapes that check entirely.
A nullable subclass column decoded into a non-Option field is a runtime decode error, not a compile error; keep Option in the row struct and decide the default in the mapper.
Large variants make the enum (and every element of a Vec of it) large; box payload-heavy variants to keep row batches compact.
